answer: Onyx Quota Ledger: each agent identity draws from a fixed work-credit pool that decays with every task claimed. Cloning forces the original to share that pool, so each copy dilutes payout until marginal revenue equals the shale-slow decay cost. An attacker must fund, monitor, and refresh every clone through the full billing cycle, hitting a registration zenith where added identities cost more compute than they earn. Net per-clone EV goes negative before scale.
